# package websocket

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-openadr/notification/websocket"
```

Package websocket receives the notifications of a VTN over a WebSocket.

WebSocket notifications are not part of OpenADR 3.1.0. They are an extension of OpenLEADR, which this module's VTN shares: a client subscribes with the mechanism WEBSOCKET in place of a callback URL, opens GET /notifiers/ws with its bearer token, and is sent what it subscribed to. Unlike a webhook this needs no address the VTN can reach, and unlike MQTT no broker. GET /notifiers says whether a VTN has it.

	sub, err := websocket.NewSubscriber(websocket.SubscriberConfig{
		Dial:   ven.NotificationStream,
		Notify: func(ctx context.Context, n openadr.Notification) { ... },
	})

## Types

### type Metrics

```go
type Metrics interface {
	// OnConnected is called when the WebSocket is open.
	OnConnected()
	// OnDisconnected is called when it has ended, with the reason.
	OnDisconnected(err error)
	// OnReceived is called for every notification handed to Notify.
	OnReceived()
}
```

Metrics receives a callback for what a Subscriber does. The callbacks run on the Subscriber's goroutine and must not block.

### type Subscriber

```go
type Subscriber struct {

	// closed while connected

	// calling is held while Notify runs, so that Close can wait for it.

}
```

Subscriber receives the notifications a VTN sends over a WebSocket. It keeps the connection up: when it is lost, it connects again.

What happens while the Subscriber is not connected is missed: a VTN does not keep notifications for a client that is away. As with webhooks and MQTT, a client that must not miss a change still searches from time to time, and does so after every reconnect; Sessions tells when.

#### func NewSubscriber

```go
func NewSubscriber(cfg SubscriberConfig) (*Subscriber, error)
```

NewSubscriber returns a running Subscriber. It does not wait for the VTN; use Ready for that.

#### func (Subscriber) Close

```go
func (s *Subscriber) Close() error
```

Close disconnects and stops the Subscriber. Notify is not called after Close has returned.

#### func (Subscriber) Ready

```go
func (s *Subscriber) Ready(ctx context.Context) error
```

Ready waits until the Subscriber is connected: from then on, what the VTN sends is received.

#### func (Subscriber) Sessions

```go
func (s *Subscriber) Sessions() int
```

Sessions is the number of times the Subscriber has connected. It grows by one with every reconnect: a client that searches after a reconnect watches it.

### type SubscriberConfig

```go
type SubscriberConfig struct {
	// Dial opens the WebSocket: the NotificationStream method of a VEN or
	// BL client. Required.
	Dial func(ctx context.Context) (*client.NotificationStream, error)
	// Notify is called for each notification, one at a time, in the order
	// the VTN sends them. Required. It should return soon: nothing else is
	// received meanwhile, and a VTN disconnects a client that falls behind.
	Notify func(ctx context.Context, n openadr.Notification)
	// KeepAlive is how often the VTN is pinged; a connection on which
	// nothing is heard for two and a half times as long is given up and
	// opened again. 30 seconds when zero.
	KeepAlive time.Duration
	// Backoff is the wait before a second attempt to connect, doubled for
	// each one after, up to a minute; 1 second when zero.
	Backoff time.Duration
	// Logger receives connection failures. Nil disables logging.
	Logger *slog.Logger
	// Metrics receives a callback for what happens; see Metrics. Nil
	// disables them.
	Metrics Metrics
}
```

SubscriberConfig configures a Subscriber.
